_comment: Read-back for every mutating admin.ops operation (fixtures/admin-bodies.json, op.mutating == true).
A write cell that only checked its own response could pass a 1.6.0 that answers 200 and writes
nothing. This file says, for each operationId, what GET a real write must show up in — the
natural read of the resource the write just touched. enumerate-cells.py turns each entry into a
`request.post` follow-up GET on that op's `ok` cell (and its idempotent-replay copy, if any); the
recorder runs it AFTER the after-effects snapshot and stores the normalized result as
`effects.readback`. An operation with no readable resource is listed with kind `none` and a
one-line reason instead of a GET.
same     GET the exact path the write used (PUT/PATCH/DELETE on a named resource)
parent   GET the write's path with its last /segment removed (a sub-resource verb like
.../revoke, .../rotate, or .../settings acts ON a resource one level up)
fixed    GET a fixed path unrelated to the write's own path (a collection/list/effective view)
resource GET a path built from the write's OWN response body via a {RESP:/pointer} placeholder
(a POST that mints a new name/id: the driver fills the placeholder from the response
JSON it just captured, e.g. {RESP:/id} -> the minted key id)
none     no GET reflects this write; `reason` says why

PostAuthCacheFlush.reason: flushes an in-process auth cache; no GET exposes cache contents or a flush counter

PostSigningKeyRotate.reason: 1.5.5 rotates nothing (reports the current kid only, per its own notes); the kid itself has no GET and is never a secret to read back

PostRestart.reason: drains both listeners and exits the process; there is no later request to make against the same instance
